title: France: Partial curfews issued in Paris, Nice after unrest
summary: French authorities imposed curfews in parts of several cities on Monday night after cost-of-living and anti-government protests descended into rioting and looting over the weekend. DW has the latest.

image.caption: Local authorities in France imposed curfews in several cities after violent protests on SaturdayImage: Camilla Baronetto/LiveMedia/ipa-agency/picture alliance

blocks.text: Are there more protests planned in France?

blocks.caption: Rioting on the weekend overshadowed demonstrations against rising costs of livingImage: Jerome Gilles/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: The answer is yes. French unions have called for a new round of rallies on November 5.
Earlier on Monday, French President Emmanuel Macron blamed organized ultraleft groups for the rioting and looting on Saturday.
Prime Minister Sebastian Lecornu said after an emergency cabinet meeting on Monday that he was "fully resolved to restore public order."
He called for imposing localized curfews, as is in place overnight into Tuesday (see below), but said there was "no question" of imposing a full curfew on entire cities.
But Lecornu refused to rule out declaring a state of emergency, which would give authorities sweeping powers to restrict public gatherings.
